        prompt="Make the fix directly. You have the root-cause statement, the proposed fix approach, and the confirmed reproduction steps.\n\nEdit the code so the root cause is corrected at its source. Keep the change minimal and localized — this path was chosen precisely because the fix is small. Match the surrounding code's style, naming and patterns, and read the root and subdirectory CLAUDE.md files plus CONTRIBUTING.md if they exist before writing anything.\n\nAdd a REGRESSION TEST wherever the project has a test suite: one that fails on the unfixed code and passes with the fix. Put it where the project's own tests for that area live, and assert the corrected behavior rather than the internals of your fix. If the project genuinely has no test suite, say so — the verified reproduction steps become the regression check instead.\n\nDo NOT delete, disable or weaken correct behavior to make the symptom disappear, do not swallow errors, and do not special-case the one input from the bug report.         backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Verify Against The Logged Repro Steps",
        thread_id="fix-bug",
        fidelity="full",
        max_visits=8,
        prompt="Re-run the EXACT reproduction sequence that was logged earlier — the same preconditions and data, the same ordered actions, the same observation point. Do not substitute a unit test for the reproduction; the reproduction is what proves the reported bug is gone.\n\nThe fix is good only when BOTH hold: the bug is gone, AND nothing else regressed. Check for regressions by running the project's full test suite and by exercising the behavior immediately around the change — the paths that share the code you touched, and the working functionality that had to be preserved.\n\nEnd this stage as SUCCEEDED only when the reproduction no longer shows the wrong behavior and no regression appeared.         backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Re-Diagnose And Retry",
        thread_id="fix-bug",
        fidelity="full",
        max_visits=6,
        prompt="The verification failed: either the bug is still there or the fix regressed something.         type="agent",

THE ROOT CAUSE — the one-line statement from the diagnosis, plus the trace that supports it and the files and functions involved.\n\n2. THE LOGGED REPRODUCTION STEPS — preconditions and data, the ordered minimal actions, the observed wrong result and the expected result, verbatim. THE REGRESSION TEST REQUIREMENT — the plan must include a test that fails on the unfixed code and passes with the fix, wherever the project has a test suite.\n\n5. THE ESCALATION REASON — which checklist item made this large or structural, so the plan is scoped to that reality.\n\nDo not write the plan here; produce the brief."
    ]

    plan_fix [import="../facto-plan-implementation/workflow.fabro"]

    // /facto:implement bundles the review loop and PR creation, so the escalated
    // path deliberately does not re-run the review or PR sub-workflows.
    implement_fix [
        import="../facto-implement/workflow.fabro"
    ]

    verify_escalated [
        backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Verify The Escalated Fix Against The Repro Steps",
        thread_id="fix-bug",
        fidelity="full",
        max_visits=8,
        prompt="The plan has been implemented, reviewed and put into a pull request by the implementation sub-workflow. Now prove the reported bug is actually gone.\n\nRe-run the EXACT reproduction sequence that was logged earlier — the same preconditions and data, the same ordered actions, the same observation point. A passing test suite is not a substitute; the reproduction is what proves the reported bug is fixed.\n\nThe fix is good only when BOTH hold: the bug is gone, AND nothing else regressed. Run the project's full test suite and exercise the behavior around the change to confirm no working functionality was removed, disabled or weakened by the larger change.\n\nEnd this stage as SUCCEEDED when the reproduction is clean and no regression appeared. End this stage as FAILED if the symptom still appears, appears in a changed form, or any previously working behavior broke — and say precisely which, with evidence."
    ]

    escalated_fix [
        backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Correct The Escalated Fix",
        max_visits=6,
        prompt="The verification of the implemented plan failed. If a regression appeared, identify the behavior that broke and restore it without reintroducing the bug — the no-regression constraint is absolute. Keep the correction scoped: amend the existing work, do not start a parallel approach.\n\nRun the project's build, lint and test commands over what you changed, and add or extend the regression test if the failure revealed a gap in it.\n\nCount the fix attempts made so far against the maximum number of fix attempts, which defaults to 5 unless the caller specified another number. End this stage as SUCCEEDED if attempts remain and you made a correction to verify. End this stage as FAILED if the budget is exhausted — the workflow then stops and reports honestly rather than thrashing."
    ]

    commit_escalated [import="../facto-commit-or-amend/workflow.fabro"]

    ensure_pr_current [
        backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Phase 6: Ensure The Pull Request Is Current",
        thread_id="fix-bug",
        fidelity="full",
        prompt="The implementation sub-workflow already opened the pull request on this branch, so do not create a second one. Make sure the existing PR is current.\n\nRead it with `gh pr view --json number,url,state,title,body`. Confirm every commit on the branch is pushed — including any correction commits made while verifying — with `git status` and `git log @{u}..HEAD --oneline`, and push what is missing.     ]

    watch_ci [
        import="../facto-watch-and-fix-ci/workflow.fabro"
    ]

        backend="acp",
        acp.command="claude-agent-acp",
        type="agent",
        label="Phase 8: Summary",
        fidelity="summary:high",

PATH TAKEN — direct or escalated, and which checklist item drove it.     understand_locate -> repro
    repro -> check_repro
    check_repro -> diagnose [label="Reproduced", condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    check_repro -> cnr_report [label="Could not reproduce"]
    cnr_report -> summary

    diagnose -> assess_fix_size
    assess_fix_size -> escalated_gate [label="Large or structural", condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    assess_fix_size -> direct_gate [label="Small and localized"]

    commit_direct -> verify_direct
    verify_direct -> review_direct [label="Bug gone, no regressions", condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    verify_direct -> rediagnose_direct [label="Bug persists or regressed"]

BUG: CLI table text is unreadable on dark terminal themes.

SYMPTOM
Secondary text in `fabro` CLI tables is hardcoded to `Color::Ansi256(8)` ("bright
black" — a fixed dark grey from the palette). That assumes a light terminal
background; on a dark theme it renders nearly invisible against the background.
Reproduced by the user with `fabro workflow list`, where the DESCRIPTION column
is unreadable.

LOCATIONS — 10 occurrences in 4 files, all under
lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/commands/
  runs/list.rs         6  (lines 128, 138, 148, 178, 184, 185)
  model.rs             2  (lines 135, 138)
  workflow/list.rs     1  (line 113)
  run/checkpoints.rs   1  (line 93)

runs/list.rs is the worst case: line 178 uses Ansi256(8) as a *status* color and
line 184 suppresses bold for it, so a run status is conveyed entirely by a color
the user cannot see. This is not purely cosmetic.

SUSPECTED CAUSE
An absolute palette index is used where a terminal-relative attribute belongs.
The codebase already has the right primitive: `fabro_util::terminal::Styles::dim`
= `Style::new().dim()` at lib/foundation/fabro-util/src/terminal.rs:28. It emits
SGR 2 (faint) against the terminal's own foreground, so it adapts to the theme.
workflow/list.rs already uses `styles.dim` for the section path in
`print_section` — the table cells in the same file just don't.

OPEN QUESTION — resolve this before choosing the fix
Does cli-table 0.5's `CellStruct` expose a faint/dim attribute the way it exposes
`.bold(bool)`? Check the actual crate source in the cargo registry rather than
guessing. Three ways it can go:
  a) If CellStruct has a faint/dim attribute, use it. Cleanest.
  b) Otherwise pre-apply the dim style to the string before `.cell()`. Risk:
     cli-table's column width measurement may count the embedded ANSI escape
     codes and mis-align the table. Verify alignment if taking this path.
  c) As a last resort pick a mid-tone color readable on both light and dark
     backgrounds — but this still absolutizes what should be relative.

Note all styling here already goes through the `use_color` flag via
`color_if()`, so the no-color path is unaffected either way.

CONTRIBUTION PATH
Per CONTRIBUTING.md this qualifies as a "bug fix / small improvement" — send a
PR directly, no issue needed. The `origin` remote is the fork
carllelandtaylor/fabro; `upstream` is fabro-sh/fabro and its push URL is
DISABLED, so push branches to `origin` only. Branch from main and open the PR
against fabro-sh/fabro main, e.g.

  gh pr create --repo fabro-sh/fabro --base main --head carllelandtaylor:<branch>

REQUIRED CHECKS (CONTRIBUTING.md's list is stale relative to CI — use these)
  cargo nextest run --workspace
  cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt --check --all
  cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
The pinned nightly matters: stable rustfmt will not match CI.

VERIFICATION
No existing test covers this. Add one asserting the faint attribute (or whatever
the chosen mechanism emits) so this cannot regress. Manually verify the rendered
output against both a light and a dark terminal profile.

An absolute palette index is used where a terminal-relative attribute belongs.

## Bug
`fabro` CLI tables render secondary/status text using a hardcoded absolute palette color (`Color::Ansi256(8)`, "bright black") instead of a terminal-relative attribute. `Color::Ansi256(8)` maps to a fixed dark grey defined by the terminal's own 256-color palette entry 8, which is calibrated for light backgrounds — on dark-themed terminals it renders nearly the same shade as the background and is effectively invisible. The codebase already has the correct terminal-relative primitive (`fabro_util::terminal::Styles::dim`, which emits SGR 2 "faint" against the terminal's actual foreground color) and uses it correctly elsewhere in the very same file, but the table cells bypass it.

## Environment / preconditions
- Repo `carllelandtaylor/fabro` at commit `0abf229` (branch `fabro/run/01KZCASWWVN35FN33S9YXJ2R2C`), `fabro-cli` built via `cargo build -p fabro-cli --bin fabro` (debug profile, `target/debug/fabro`).
- Requires a real/pty terminal with color enabled (`console::colors_enabled_stderr()` / `colors_enabled()` must be true) — a `TERM` other than `dumb`, no `NO_COLOR` set, stderr/stdout attached to a tty (a plain pipe with no pty, e.g. running under `script` with the default inherited `TERM=dumb`, disables color and hides the bug).
